news_drafts.headline: Dumfries and Galloway projects £764k overspend on Supporting Learners and £253k on primary schools
news_drafts.lead:
Dumfries and Galloway Council's education service projects overspends on two budget lines for 2026/27: £764k on Supporting Learners and £253k on primary schools. The figures are in the second-quarter revenue budget monitoring report for the Education, Skills and Community Wellbeing Committee, which meets on 10 November.

Supporting Learners has a projected out-turn of £22.705m against a revised budget of £21.941m. Additional support for learning (ASL) generic support is the largest single variance. It is projected at £1.143m over its revised budget of £13.149m. Education Psychologists, Sensory Services and Targeted Support are each projected under budget.

The primary schools line, which includes Learning Centres, has a projected out-turn of £60.288m against a revised budget of £60.035m. The paper records a £1.038m budget adjustment in 2026/27 before that revised budget was set.
news_drafts.paper_title: ESCW Q2 Revenue Budget Monitoring 202627 Appendix 1

news_drafts.headline: Dumfries and Galloway: Dumfries Academy and Loreburn Primary allocation left a gap of about £10m
news_drafts.lead:
The money Dumfries and Galloway Council had agreed for Dumfries Academy and Loreburn Primary School does not cover the costs identified for the two schools, leaving a funding gap of around £10m. The figure is in an appendix to the council's capital investment programme, its planned spending on things that last, such as buildings, over the next few years.

The council's Education and Learning Committee agreed on 23 May 2024 that the existing allocation was not enough. That allocation is part of £73.975m in the programme. The appendix says: "Previously agreed capital allocation (part of the £73.975m) is not enough to cover the values identified, so Members also agreed to request the funding gap, circa £10m, from FTP committee."

FTP is the Finance, Procurement and Transformation Committee. The papers quoted here do not say how that committee responded to the request.

news_drafts.headline: Dumfries and Galloway council secures £50m Levelling Up grants but faces social care audit concerns
news_drafts.lead: The council has received over £50 million from the UK Government's Levelling Up Fund. Its capital projects — spending on buildings and other long-lived assets — are delivering on schedule: the Stranraer Watersports Hub is due to open in September, the Dalbeattie Rocks and Wheels facility is nearing completion, and the George building has attracted eight expressions of interest with a tender exercise in progress. The internal audit's overall opinion is Reasonable, meaning there is a generally sound system of governance, risk management and control in place. However, auditors have flagged two areas requiring ongoing monitoring: social care budgets and IT procurement, indicating these carry elevated risk requiring continuous attention.

findings.committee: Education, Skills and Community Wellbeing Committee
findings.paper_title: ESCW Q2 Revenue Budget Monitoring 202627 Report
findings.headline: The Scottish Government has not given details of No One Left Behind and Child Poverty funding beyond 2026/27, so resources have been held in reserves for any transition.
findings.detail: The paper says the reserves will help support any required transition or cessation of these resources and will allow continuity of support for the Employability Service. The paper does not state the amount held in reserves for this purpose.
findings.matters: Funding from central government that is not confirmed beyond the current year, with reserves set aside to cover it, is a risk that other councils' employability and anti-poverty budgets will also carry.
findings.quote: Whilst the Scottish Government have not provided details of ongoing commitments on No One Left Behind/Child Poverty funding beyond 26/27, resources have been held within reserves

findings.committee: Education, Skills and Community Wellbeing Committee
findings.paper_title: ESCW Q2 Revenue Budget Monitoring 202627 Report
findings.headline: Thriving Communities is forecast to underspend by £212k, primarily because Leisure and Sport membership income is above budgeted levels.
findings.detail: The paper says this position may improve further during the year, subject to fluctuations in customer demand. The Events service is separately forecast to underspend by £25k, and that figure may change depending on Members' decisions on the remaining Major Events funding allocations.
findings.matters: Income above budget is a source of offset that depends on demand, and other councils' leisure budgets will be watching whether membership income holds up.
findings.quote: primarily due to Leisure and Sport membership income being above budgeted levels

findings.committee: Education, Skills and Community Wellbeing Committee
findings.paper_title: ESCW Q2 Revenue Budget Monitoring 202627 Report
findings.headline: The Permanent Supply Teachers saving is being delivered earlier than anticipated, giving a £70k underspend in Directorate Education Resources.
findings.detail: The paper says the saving was originally split across two financial years and that staff moved earlier than expected, so part of the saving planned for 2027/28 has already been realised in 2026/27. Further savings are still expected in 2027/28.
findings.matters: A saving landing ahead of its schedule, with the balance still to come, is a timing change that a finance director would need to reflect in later-year savings forecasts.
findings.quote: This reflects the Permanent Supply Teachers saving being delivered earlier than anticipated.

findings.committee: Education, Skills and Community Wellbeing Committee
findings.paper_title: ESCW Q2 Revenue Budget Monitoring 202627 Report
findings.headline: ASL Generic Support is projected to exceed its recurring budget allocation by £1,055k, with £764k drawn from an agreed reserve.
findings.detail: The paper says the additional spend reflects the agreed use of non-recurring resources to enhance staffing support, with most staff now in post. Other Supporting Learners functions are forecast to underspend by £291k, which partly offsets the overspend, leaving the Supporting Learners budget forecast to break even after the reserve drawdown.
findings.matters: Using a one-off reserve to fund staffing that runs above the recurring budget means the pressure will remain when the reserve is spent, and other councils funding additional support in the same way will face the same question.
findings.figures: £1,055k over recurring budget (ASL Generic Support); £291k underspend (other Supporting Learners functions); £764k reserve drawdown; £0 estimated outturn position (Supporting Learners)
findings.quote: The ASL Generic Support budget is currently projected to exceed its recurring budget allocation by £1,055k.

findings.committee: Education, Skills and Community Wellbeing Committee
findings.paper_title: ESCW Q2 Revenue Budget Monitoring 202627 Report
findings.headline: Primary Schools is forecast to be overspent by £253k, mainly because supply teaching costs are projected to exceed the available budget.
findings.detail: The paper says the forecast includes an allowance for higher winter costs and that the position may improve if actual supply use is lower than estimated. It also says Primary Schools' cost pressures are currently being offset by underspends elsewhere in the directorate.
findings.matters: Supply teaching costs are a recurring pressure that other councils' education budgets will also face, and the paper shows it being absorbed by underspends rather than by a separate funding decision.
findings.quote: The main factor contributing to this overspend is the cost of supply teaching staff, which is projected to exceed the available budget.

daily_post.headline: Structures has a 2026/27 forecast outturn of £599,428 against a £480,000 revised budget, a forecast variance of £119,428.
daily_post.lead: A forecast above budget on a structures programme is a cost pressure that finance officers at other councils with similar bridge and structures work will recognise.
